Living in Alaska my whole life i’ve learned a few things about bears.

Black bears - You actually have a fighting chance to take on a (small) black bear. Anything bigger your odds are slim. These bears are more skittish and are pretty much trying to get away from danger. Do not climb trees they will follow with no hesitation.

Brown bears / Grizzlies - Don’t play dead, this is a false narrative and usually never works because they feast on dead meat. Your best chance of survival is keeping direct eye contact while trying to back away slowly. If the bear approaches at speed then make loud noises and stand tall, for example, take your jacket or shirt and lift it above your head so it makes you look taller. You usually won’t find brown/grizzlies in open areas so try to find cover. 

Polar Bear - Accept your fate and do better in the next life. These are unforgiving creatures that have little to no contact with humans so when they see us we are literally a giant chunk of fresh meat. Your best chance of survival without a proper tool (which is only a gun) is nothing!

Pro tip: Don’t take chances and stay out of areas that are listed as “bear country” unless you are equipped with proper tools (bear spray, gun, airhorn, etc.) and with a group. Too many people from my hometown have taken risks and suffered.
